items.title: 67426_Hayes Pillars oral history interview
items.q: we got along this way. He took care of all the business of the band... I was in charge of the music end of the band.

ctx.x: To me, that's a long time for two people to work together and have a band and maintain the kind of relationship that you and Mr. Jeter maintained.

Yeah. Well, Jeta -- I tell you, we got along this way. He took care of all the business of the band, paid the guys off. I was in charge of the music end of the band. If I saw a musician I thought the band -- was good enough for the band, I picked him out and tell everybody, I think we should get this guy, get that guy. I did the recruiting. And a lot of times we would have a few arguments. And things just weren't rosy all the time.

But I understood him and I think he understood me, see. And my brother, Charles, was a great help with us, although he didn't share in the gravy of the band. There was very little gravy for the band, you see. But there were times when we would give him a little extra or something here or something there, see.
